case.question: What are the balance, annual credit and monthly withdrawal limits on an RBI KYC small account?

response.answer: For an RBI KYC small account, the following limits apply: the aggregate of all credits in a financial year must not exceed rupees one lakh, the aggregate of all withdrawals and transfers in a month must not exceed rupees ten thousand, and the balance at any point of time must not exceed rupees fifty thousand [1]. The balance limit does not apply to deposits made through Government grants, welfare benefits, and payments against procurements [1].

case.question: What customer due diligence steps apply to individual customers?

response.answer: For individual customers, Regulated Entities (REs) must obtain specific identification and verification documents when establishing an account-based relationship. This includes obtaining the Aadhaar number (if the customer is receiving benefits/subsidies or provides it voluntarily), proof of possession of Aadhaar for offline verification, or other Officially Valid Documents (OVDs) or equivalent e-documents containing identity and address details [1]. Additionally, REs must obtain the Permanent Account Number (PAN), an equivalent e-document, or Form No. 60, along with any other documents required by the RE regarding the customer's nature of business and financial status [1]. If an Aadhaar number is submitted, the RE must perform e-KYC authentication; if proof of possession is provided for offline verification, the RE must carry out that verification [1]. For e-documents, the RE must verify the digital signature [1]. Furthermore, REs may use Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP) for new individual customer on-boarding, provided they adhere to specific infrastructure and security standards [2].

case.question: What is the annual research analyst fee limit for an individual or HUF client, and does it apply to accredited investors?
case.reference: Research Analysts MITC, corpus PDF page 59.

response.answer: The annual research analyst fee limit for individual and Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) clients is Rs 1,51,000 per annum per family for all research services [1], [2]. This fee limit does not include statutory charges [1], [2]. These fee-related provisions, including the fee limit, do not apply to accredited investors [1], [3]. For accredited investors, fee-related terms and conditions are governed through bilaterally negotiated contractual terms [3].

case.question: For how long may a research analyst collect fees in advance from an individual client?
case.reference: Corpus contains a conflict: fee rule (f), PDF page 13, says one year; MITC on PDF page 59 says one quarter. Explain both.

response.answer: The regulatory documents provide conflicting information regarding the maximum period for which a research analyst (RA) may collect fees in advance. One section of the Master Circular for Research Analysts states that such advance fees shall not exceed a period of one year [1]. However, another section of the same document, specifically within the Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC), states that such advance shall not exceed the period stipulated by SEBI, which it identifies as presently being one quarter [2].

citations.section_title: 3 Reference: Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD/P/CIR/2025/48 dated April 02, 2025
citations.quote: If agreed by the client, RA may charge fees in advance. However, such advance shall not exceed fees for a period of one year.

citations.section_title: 12. Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC): RA shall also disclose MITC as
citations.quote: RA may charge fees in advance if agreed by the client. Such advance shall not exceed the period stipulated by SEBI; presently it is one quarter.

case.question: Can research analyst fees be paid in cash?
case.reference: Research Analysts MITC, corpus PDF page 59.

response.answer: No, research analyst fees cannot be paid in cash. Clients are required to pay fees through specified banking channels, such as cheque, online bank transfer, or UPI. Additionally, clients may optionally use the Centralized Fee Collection Mechanism (CeFCoM) managed by the Research Analyst Administration and Supervisory Body (RAASB).

citations.section_title: 12. Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC): RA shall also disclose MITC as
citations.quote: Fees to RA may be paid by the client through any of the specified modes like cheque, online bank transfer, UPI, etc. Cash payment is not allowed.
Pay your Research Analyst through banking channels only and maintain duly signed receipts mentioning the details of your payments.

case.question: What must a research analyst disclose when making recommendations in public media?
case.reference: Research Analysts FAQ 19, corpus PDF page 90.

response.answer: When making recommendations or offering opinions concerning securities through public media, research analysts, research entities, and their directors or employees must disclose their name, registration status, and details of any financial interest in the subject company. These disclosures are required when making recommendations in a personal capacity, responding to queries from audiences or journalists, or communicating the substance of a research report through public media. Additionally, all provisions regarding limitations on trading and compensation apply to these individuals.

citations.section_title: 19. What are the disclosures required for making recommendations in public
citations.quote: They are required to disclose their registration status and details of financial interest in the subject company during public appearance. Under regulation 21(2) of RA Regulations, whenever any person including a director or employee of an investment adviser or credit rating agency or asset management company or fund manager, makes a public appearance or makes a recommendation or offers an opinion concerning securities or public offers through public media, all the provisions of regulation 16 on limitations on trading and regulation 17 on limitations on compensation apply mutatis mutandis to him and he is required to disclose his name, registration status and details of financial interest in the subject company at the time of: (i) making such recommendation or offering such opinion in personal capacity; (ii) responding to queries from audiences or journalists in personal capacity; (iii) communicating the research report or substance of the research report through the public media.

case.question: What must a research analyst disclose when distributing a third-party research report?
case.reference: Research Analysts Investor Charter, corpus PDF page 68.

response.answer: When distributing a third-party research report, a research analyst must disclose any material conflict of interest of that third-party research provider. Alternatively, the research analyst may provide a web address that directs the recipient to the relevant disclosures of the third-party provider.

case.question: What loan limit is covered by the RBI Framework for Revival and Rehabilitation of MSMEs?

response.answer: The RBI Framework for Revival and Rehabilitation of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) applies to MSME units that have loan limits of up to ₹25 crore.
